## Source 1 — LTS-VoiceAgent: A Listen-Think-Speak Framework for Efficient Streaming Voice Interaction via Semantic Triggering and Incremental Reasoning (arXiv 2601.19952, submitted 26 Jan 2026)

**Type:** Academic paper (arXiv cs.Sound, 2026)
**Headline:** "LTS-VoiceAgent: A Listen-Think-Speak Framework for Efficient Streaming Voice Interaction via Semantic Triggering and Incremental Reasoning"

### Verbatim excerpts (from abstract):
> "Real-time voice agents face a dilemma: end-to-end models often lack deep reasoning, while cascaded pipelines incur high latency by executing ASR, LLM reasoning, and TTS strictly in sequence, unlike human conversation where listeners often start thinking before the speaker finishes."
> "Since cascaded architectures remain the dominant choice for complex tasks, existing cascaded streaming strategies attempt to reduce this latency via mechanical segmentation (e.g., fixed ch[unk]...)"

### Pain points (verbatim audience language):
- Cascaded pipeline latency is the structural problem
- "Mechanical segmentation" (fixed chunks) is the wrong pattern
- "Semantic triggering" — trigger LLM on semantic end-of-turn, not on chunk boundaries

### Why this works:
This is the **freshest academic formalization** of the persona's Example 9 latency-tuning insight. The paper ID (arXiv 2601.19952) and the framework name (Listen-Think-Speak) are the named-anchor data points. **The Scribe should cite the paper ID and framework name exactly. The semantic-triggering insight extends the persona's existing "the math is the product" framing with academic pedigree.**

## Source 2 — Toward Low-Latency End-to-End Voice Agents for Telecommunications Using Streaming ASR, Quantized LLMs, and Real-Time TTS (arXiv 2508.04721, submitted 5 Aug 2025)

**Type:** Academic paper (arXiv cs.Sound, 2025)
**Headline:** "Toward Low-Latency End-to-End Voice Agents for Telecommunications Using Streaming ASR, Quantized LLMs, and Real-Time TTS"

### Verbatim excerpts (from abstract):
> "We introduce a low-latency telecom AI voice agent pipeline for real-time, interactive telecommunications use, enabling advanced voice AI for call center automation, intelligent IVR (Interactive Voice Response), and AI-driven customer support."
> "The solution is built for telecom, combining four specialized models by NetoAI: TSLAM, a 4-bit quantized Telecom-Specific Large Language Model (LLM); T-VEC, a Telecom-Specific Embedding Model; TTE, a Telecom-Specific Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model; and T-Synth, a Te[lecom-Specific TTS]..."

### Pain points (verbatim audience language):
- 4 specialized models stacked (TSLAM + T-VEC + TTE + T-Synth) is the named-anchor pattern
- 4-bit quantization (TSLAM) is the named-anchor optimization
- Telecom-specific is the named-anchor domain (parallel to trades-specific)

### Why this works:
The 4-model cascade (TSLAM + T-VEC + TTE + T-Synth) is the **named-anchor pattern for vertical-specific voice agents**. Pairs with Source 1 (LTS-VoiceAgent academic framework) for the "academic formalization + vendor implementation" two-source arc.
